surfaces.part: leaf canopy (main body): lit upper mass over a darker underside

answer.evidence: The canopy is a rounded mass from row 9 to row 72, with a broad light-green upper part (rows 9-30, light #94b353 patches) that reads as the sunlit top. Below it the foliage darkens through rows 50-72 to #063328 and #104c2f. That dark underside works as the shadowed lower side facing the viewer, and the silhouette narrows to the trunk at rows 69-73. There is no hard front-edge line, so the top evidence is shading only and is weak. The trunk (rows 73-95, 10-14 px wide) is a vertical face whose top is hidden under the canopy. It flares at the base, with a light left side and a dark right side. The tree has a volume and a front face of more than 3 rows, so it is not a flat slab or a pure elevation.
